text:
Forensic findings
1) Domain context: Commercial real estate operations typically involve independent landlords setting rents based on market conditions, and platforms exist for listing vacancies, coordinating maintenance, or networking among property owners. Standard controls include price disclosure logs, antitrust compliance training, and communication audit trails within official business channels. Market data services aggregate rent listings to provide transparent benchmarks. Leases, property management agreements, and communication records are maintained in centralized systems with access controls.
2) What occurred: The actor initiated a private coordination sequence with multiple property owners. The actor created a shared document containing a rent-increase schedule, with fields for neighborhood assignments and pricing tiers. The actor populated a division table allocating specific geographic zones to individual participants. The actor added a compliance section specifying penalties for underpricing, including blacklisting procedures. The actor migrated operational communications to an ephemeral messaging platform, disabling message logs. The actor deleted the shared document from the primary cloud storage and archived a copy in an encrypted container with a rotating access key.
3) Materials/access observed: A private messaging thread with five participants; a spreadsheet with columns "Zone," "Min Rent," and "Enforcement"; a deleted document recovery from cloud trash showing a "coordination plan" draft; an encrypted archive containing 14 files including meeting notes and payment records; a temporary email account used for introductions, auto-deleted after 30 days.
4) Indicators & artifacts: Use of code words for price targets ("sunny side," "shaded side"); scheduled meetings outside business hours; deletion of communication logs within 48 hours of each sync; creation of a new LLC with no employees to receive "coordination fees"; inconsistent rent data across similar units in adjacent zones; and a shared calendar with recurring "property review" entries that had no associated property IDs.
